jobs.title: Campus Ministry Director at First Presbyterian Church of Marquette
jobs.description: Employer: First Presbyterian Church of Marquette Expires: 10/30/2026 Schedule: Part-time (10-15 hours). Hours are flexible with some Sundays required. This is a 9 month position approximately mid-August through mid-May. The church would consider the possibility of a Full-Time position for the right candidate who is also interested in the Director of Spiritual Formation and Outreach role. Working Relationships: The Campus Ministry Director (CMD) reports directly to the Pastor. Works collaboratively with the Pastor, campus ministry colleagues, students, staff and the Session. The CMD will also recruit, equip and work alongside a team of volunteers/lay leaders. I. Summary: First Presbyterian Church of Marquette (FPC) is seeking a CMD with a vision for campus ministry. We are a small church of approximately 125 members located on the shores of Lake Superior in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan. Marquette is well-known as a desirable place to live for its outdoor beauty and adventures and for being ranked in the top ten best small town cultural scenes by USA Today. We have a strong desire for campus ministry outreach to Northern Michigan University (NMU) located one mile from the church. NMU is home to 7,200 students. The need for a Christ-centered student ministry that affirms women in leadership, LGBTQ+ students, positive mental health, stewardship and creation care, and values informed biblical, social and political engagement is evident.This position is responsible for the development of such a ministry in collaboration with the existing ecumenical ministry of Sacred Space (which has historically included four mainline denominations: Episcopal, Methodist, ELCA and PCUSA. Sacred Space is in the midst of some transition, so there is plenty of opportunity to build anew. We seek a Director aligned with the inclusive theology of the PC(USA) who embodies the gracious hospitality, teachings, and love of Christ. In addition, the CMD will have a visible presence within the FPC congregation, worship, and outreach events. II. Our Vision & Values: FPC adopted a new Vision & Values Statement in 2025. We imagined the following picture of what First Presbyterian Church might be like by 2029 with God’s grace and our obedience: We are a community of faith withWorship that is vibrant and diverseCommunity that is authentic and inclusive Spiritual Formation that is holistic and rooted in ScriptureMission that is focused on the marginalized and ranges from local to global III. Primary Responsibilities1. Engage in & Sustain Campus Ministry at NMUEngage in the existing ecumenical Campus Ministry: Sacred Space which includes four mainline denominations: Episcopal, Methodist, ELCA and PCUSA. Build relationships with students and develop their faith formation. Offer regular gatherings for study, worship, service, and fellowship (including occasional retreats at local church camp Presbytery Point and mission trips). 2. Be the Connection between Students and the CongregationRegularly communicate the campus ministry happenings to the church. Build relationships between college students and the congregation. (Mentors, adopt-a-family or grandparent, etc.) Participate and encourage student participation in community outreach events when appropriate. Assist in worship leadership occasionally. V. Qualifications:Background in Christian education, ministry, missional outreach or related field. Theological training preferred. Strong relational, communication and organizational skills. Background check required. Mandated PC(USA) Boundary Training upon hire. Commitment to PC(USA) theology and mission. Salary: Commensurate with experience and hours desired. Range: $10-12K. We offer a generous PTO package and holiday pay. VI. How to Apply:Please send your cover letter, resume, and references to the Church: firstpresbyterianmqt@gmail.com Applications will be reviewed on July 20th and continue to be accepted until the position is filled.

You will be able to work in a supportive small team atmosphere while also working as part of a larger organization that is a leader within the mental health care industry. The Mobile Crisis Intervention (MCI) program provides crisis and behavioral health assessment, intervention, and stabilization services 24 hours per day, seven days per week, and 365 days per year (24/7/365) for individuals who are experiencing a behavioral health crisis.The mission of MCI is to respond rapidly, assess effectively, and deliver a course of treatment intended to promote recovery, ensure safety, and stabilize the crisis in a manner that allows the person served to receive medically necessary services in the community, or if medically necessary, in an inpatient or 24-hour diversionary level of care. The Triage Clinician – MCI works as a member of a multi-disciplinary team that includes physicians, nurses, behavioral health clinicians, certified peer specialists, family partners and recovery coaches, to provide core services including crisis assessment, intervention, stabilization, and post-stabilization. Key activities are summarized below.MAJOR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES (include, but are not limited to):Bring an innovation mindset to materials development – researching and piloting new formats, jobs.title: Clinical Director at Family Pride of Northeast Ohio
jobs.description: Employer: Family Pride of Northeast Ohio Expires: 10/30/2026 Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Make an Impact.Family Pride of Northeast Ohio is looking for an experienced, passionate behavioral health leader to join our team as Clinical Director.This is more than a clinical leadership position—it is an opportunity to shape the future of behavioral health services across our organization and the communities we serve.The Clinical Director provides organization-wide clinical leadership and strategic direction for Family Pride’s mental health, substance use disorder (SUD), and prevention services. This individual will champion quality care, develop strong clinical leaders, drive innovation, strengthen programs, and help ensure that the services we provide continue to meet the evolving needs of individuals, families, and communities.If you are a confident clinical leader who enjoys developing people, building programs, solving problems, using data to drive decisions, and creating meaningful change, we would love to hear from you.Why Join Family Pride?At Family Pride, we appreciate and value our staff. We believe strong organizations are built by strong people, and we are committed to creating a workplace where leaders can make a difference while maintaining balance and professional growth.Full-Time Benefits Include:· Your Birthday Off – Take your birthday off to celebrate!· 3 Floating Holidays of your choice· 8 Paid Holidays· 120 Hours of Combined Sick & Vacation Time· Health Insurance· Dental Insurance· Vision Insurance· Short-Term Disability· 3% SIMPLE IRA Match· Student Loan Contribution· A supportive, collaborative work environment· Opportunities for professional growth and leadership developmentABOUT THE ROLEThe Clinical Director serves as a key member of Family Pride's leadership team and works closely with Senior Leadership to align clinical priorities with organizational strategy, community needs, financial sustainability, staffing, and operational capacity.The position will provide leadership, coaching, accountability, and strategic direction to clinical supervisors and program leaders while strengthening collaboration across Family Pride's programs, locations, and service areas.The Clinical Director will help build a culture where quality, innovation, accountability, professional growth, and compassionate care are at the center of everything we do. This is an organization-wide clinical leadership position and does not carry a routine clinical caseload.WHAT YOU'LL DOLead Clinical Strategy· Provide organization-wide clinical leadership and strategic direction for Family Pride's mental health, SUD treatment, and prevention services.· Ensure clinical services align with Family Pride's mission, vision, strategic goals, and the needs of the communities we serve.· Oversee the planning, development, implementation, and continuous improvement of clinical programs and services.· Identify opportunities to expand and strengthen clinical programming and partnerships.Develop & Inspire Clinical Leaders· Provide direction, coaching, support, and accountability to clinical supervisors and program leaders.· Develop strong clinical leaders who effectively support, develop, and hold their teams accountable.· Strengthen collaboration and communication among clinical teams across Family Pride's locations and service areas.· Create opportunities for shared learning, professional development, and the exchange of best practices.· Establish and oversee an agency-wide clinical training plan focused on evidence-based practices and quality care.Champion Quality & Outcomes· Establish and monitor clinical and program performance indicators, including quality, productivity, access, outcomes, documentation, and client engagement.· Use data and performance measures to identify trends, address concerns, and guide continuous improvement.· Oversee clinical documentation, quality assurance, and clinical risk management systems.· Promote a culture of accountability and continuous quality improvement.Drive Innovation· Support the adoption of technology, clinical tools, systems, and innovative approaches that improve access, efficiency, documentation, quality, and client experience.· Stay informed about emerging behavioral health practices, trends, funding priorities, and system developments.· Identify innovative service models that respond to changing community needs.Ensure Compliance & Excellence· Provide leadership for clinical compliance with CARF, OhioDBH, payer requirements, applicable laws and regulations, and professional standards.· Ensure clinical programs and services meet organizational and regulatory expectations.· Partner with leadership to identify and address compliance, quality, and risk-management needs.Collaborate Across the Organization· Work closely with Senior Leadership to align clinical priorities with organizational strategy, financial sustainability, staffing, technology, and resource allocation.· Serve as the key clinical liaison to the Board of Directors and present clinical programming and strategic priorities at Board and Program Resources Committee meetings.· Build strong relationships across departments, locations, programs, and service areas.Be a Community Leader· Represent Family Pride professionally throughout the behavioral health and broader community.· Build meaningful relationships with behavioral health, healthcare, education, government, and community partners.· Participate in professional organizations, community initiatives, coalitions, conferences, and other opportunities that strengthen Family Pride's presence and impact.Requirements What we are looking for:We are seeking a leader who brings experience, confidence, compassion, accountability, and vision to the role.Required Qualifications· Master's degree or higher in social work, counseling, psychology, or a related behavioral health field from an accredited college or university.· Current independent clinical licensure in the State of Ohio with appropriate supervisory designation, such as LISW-S or LPCC-S, as applicable.· Minimum of 7 years of progressive clinical experience in behavioral health, including mental health and/or substance use disorder services.· Minimum of 3 years of experience providing clinical supervision and leading clinical teams, programs, or services.· Demonstrated experience in clinical program development, quality improvement, compliance, and/or organizational leadership.· Experience using data and performance measures to evaluate clinical quality, outcomes, productivity, and program effectiveness.· Strong knowledge of behavioral health regulations, accreditation standards, payer requirements, and evidence-based practices.· Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships with employees, leadership, community partners, and professional organizations.· Strong written and verbal communication, problem-solving, decision-making, organizational, and time-management skills.· Ability to prioritize competing responsibilities and lead effectively in a changing environment.Preferred QualitiesThe ideal Clinical Director is someone who:· Leads with purpose. You understand that effective leadership starts with relationships, trust, and accountability.· Develops people. You enjoy mentoring supervisors and helping clinical professionals become strong leaders.· Thinks strategically. You can see the big picture while understanding how day-to-day clinical operations impact the organization.· Embraces innovation. You are willing to challenge "the way we've always done it" and explore better ways to serve clients and support staff.· Use data to make decisions. You understand that quality care and organizational success go hand in hand with measurable outcomes.· Builds connections. You know that strong partnerships with staff, community organizations, healthcare providers, schools, government agencies, and other stakeholders make our work stronger.· Cares about the mission. Most importantly, you believe in making a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals, families, and communities. Work Environment & TravelThe Clinical Director primarily works in a professional office environment and regularly interacts with employees, leadership, clients, community partners, and other stakeholders. Work may occur across Family Pride locations and in community settings as needed. Remote work may be available when appropriate. The position requires the ability to sit, stand, walk, and move throughout office and community environments for extended periods and to use standard office equipment and technology. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position. The Clinical Director must be able to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, and electronically and review clinical, regulatory, organizational, and data-related materials. This is a full-time leadership position. Flexibility may be required for occasional evening or weekend meetings, community events, trainings, conferences, and other organizational activities. Regular travel between Family Pride locations and service areas is required. Occasional travel throughout the region and Ohio may be required. Reliable transportation and the ability to travel as required by the position are necessary.Ready to Lead with Purpose?If you are looking for an opportunity to lead clinical excellence, develop people, shape programs, and make a lasting impact in behavioral health, we invite you to join Family Pride.Bring your experience. Bring your vision. Help us continue to grow, innovate, and make a difference.

The Master’s level Clinician is an integral part of the Community Behavioral Health Center’s (CBHC) Mobile Crisis Intervention program. MCI provides crisis intervention services 7 days per week, 24 hours per day either on-site or mobile to any individual experiencing a mental health and/or substance use challenges. The mission of the MCI is to respond rapidly, assess effectively, and deliver a course of treatment intended to promote recovery, ensure safety, and stabilize the crisis in a manner that allows the person served to receive medically necessary services in the community, or if medically necessary, in an inpatient or 24-hour diversionary level of care. The MCI clinician works as a member of a multi-disciplinary team that includes physicians, nurses, behavioral health clinicians, certified peer specialists, and recovery coaches, to provide core services including crisis assessment, intervention, stabilization, and post-stabilization. Primary duties include telephone triage, crisis intervention (including evaluation, stabilization, referral and follow-up) on-site and in the community. In addition, the MCI clinician serves as a liaison between the MCI team and community providers for continuity of care. The Master’s level Clinician is an integral part of the Community Behavioral Health Center’s (CBHC) Mobile Crisis Intervention program. MCI provides crisis intervention services 7 days per week, 24 hours per day either on-site or mobile to any individual experiencing a mental health and/or substance use challenges. jobs.title: Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) at Alpaca Health
jobs.description: Employer: Alpaca Health Expires: 10/30/2026 Alpaca HealthWork Location: In Person If you want work that challenges you, changes lives, and builds a real career, this is it. For many of our roles you don’t need your RBT certification to apply. What matters most is that you love working with kids, you’re dependable, and you’re ready to show up. Some roles do require an active certification, but if you’re not certified yet, we’ll help you find your path to getting there.Alpaca Health is a multi-state network of independent ABA therapists, working in homes, schools, and daycares. We hire certified RBTs and motivated people ready to become one. Either way, you’ll work alongside a dedicated BCBA who mentors you from day one, not a manager, not a corporate supervisor. Two ways to joinAlready an RBTActive RBT certificationStart working and earning right awayWork with clients in your regionA path toward BCBA if you want itNot certified yetA clear path to becoming an RBT, with a BCBA mentor from day oneMany practices in our network reimburse RBT training and pay you during hands-on learning, and we’ll help match you with the right fitSupport as you prepare for and sit for your certification exam The jobYou’ll work one-on-one with kids with autism in their homes, classrooms, and communities. Every day is different. You’ll follow a personalized plan from your BCBA, implement behavior strategies, collect data, and build the consistent relationships that help kids grow. Your BCBA is closely involved and reachable, so there’s no guessing and no flying solo. What’s in it for you:$20–$27/hour, based on experience and locationDirect mentorship from a dedicated BCBA, not managers or a corporate chain of commandFull-time or part-time (some flexibility across mornings, afternoons, and evenings is needed to meet client needs; not sure if a schedule fits? Just ask, we have many)Career growth support, including a path toward BCBA certificationDepending on the practice: training reimbursement and paid hands-on learning for those earning their certification You’re a good fit if you:Genuinely enjoy working with children, especially kids who need extra patience and creativityHave an active RBT certification, or the drive to earn oneHave reliable availability across mornings, afternoons, or evenings, since our clients count on consistencyCome from education, childcare, psychology, social work, or any role where you showed up for kidsHave reliable transportation to reach client homes and schoolsCan keep up physically, getting on the floor, moving around, staying active (able to lift ~50 lbs)Are at least 18, have a high school diploma or equivalent, and can pass a background check Why Alpaca HealthWe’re not a big clinic chain. We’re a network of independent therapists who chose this work because they believe in it, and we match every RBT with a BCBA who mentors, not manages. We match families with providers who have availability now, and we work where families actually are. If you want a career where you see the results of your work every single day, this is it. Ready? Apply now.Not sure if you qualify? Apply anyway and tell us about yourself. We’d rather talk to one more curious person than miss someone great.

jobs.description: Employer: USA Today - Election Team Expires: 10/30/2026 USA Today Co is currently trying to find stringers to go to local municipal offices or polling places and report election results to us throughout the evening on November 3rd for the General Election. It is a great opportunity for students to get involved in the electoral process and see the role the media plays in elections. It is also completely nonpartisan, only focused on getting election results to the public quickly and accurately. Location: Positions available in Amesbury and Cape CodDate: Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026Hours: 7:45 PM until final results are releasedPay: Flat fee equal to $125Job Description: USA Today Stringers are a valuable part of our election results collection operation. As a stringer, your main responsibility is to report results to USA Today via the web using your smartphone. In some cases, phone calls may be necessary instead. Results will be released by election officials periodically, and stringers will upload the new results as quickly and accurately as possible after receiving the update. They will also remain on site to answer any questions USA Today may have about when or how results are being released. This position typically takes around 4 hours but could go longer, and stringers should be prepared to stay until the election official indicates that no more results will be released this evening, or until your coordinator dismisses you. There will be a short but mandatory training, as well as a rehearsal, prior to election day that will cover how to report results, how to interact with officials, and how to get paid. Potential for becoming a regular election night stringer in your area is very high, so long as the job is done well. If interested, please reach out as soon as possible to ensure a position is still available in your area. If interested, please email your name, phone number, and zip code to rboike@usatodayco.com.Requirements: Smartphone, transportation, ability to quickly and accurately record results to report.

Desired Skills & Experience:High School Diploma or equivalent required. An Associate’s Degree in Education is preferred.Minimum of two (2) years of experience working with children under the age of 13.Current Pediatrics CPR or First Aid certifications preferred. General knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.Strong interpersonal skills, leadership qualities, and comfortable working with diverse youth and adults.Y Afterschool programs operate Monday through Friday from 2:30 p.m. - 6:00 p.m. and during public-school breaks. jobs.title: Early Childhood Teacher of Students with Severe Disabilities - $3,000 Sign-On Bonus! - ASL Proficient at The Children's Center for Communication/ Beverly School Deaf
jobs.description: Employer: The Children's Center for Communication/ Beverly School Deaf Expires: 10/30/2026 Early Childhood Teacher of Students with Severe DisabilitiesBeverly, Massachusetts | Full-TimeThis full-time faculty position follows CCCBSD’s 204-day school calendar (37.5 hours per week). The annual schedule includes one orientation day in July, followed by 23 summer program days (Monday–Thursday) scheduled at approximately 30 hours per week during the summer session in July and August. The calendar also includes one additional orientation day in September and 181 school days during the academic year (Monday–Friday).Faculty benefit from a school-based calendar while participating in meaningful professional development, collaboration, and program planning throughout the year.Make a Lasting ImpactAt The Children’s Center for Communication/Beverly School for the Deaf (CCCBSD), we provide transformative, person-centered education and services for Deaf and/or disabled individuals in a language-rich, inclusive setting. We envision a world where Deaf and disabled individuals, their families, and communities thrive with dignity, purpose, and joy. As an Early Childhood Teacher of Students with Severe Disabilities, you will help shape meaningful educational experiences for young students with diverse developmental, physical, communication, and behavioral needs. You will empower students to grow academically, socially, emotionally, and communicatively through accessible, individualized instruction.Your ImpactAs an Early Childhood Teacher of Students with Severe Disabilities, you will lead a small classroom of approximately 3–5 students, supported by an intensive faculty-to-student ratio and a highly collaborative team. You will provide adapted curriculum, individualized classroom instruction, therapeutic support, and communication-focused learning opportunities designed around each student's unique strengths, needs, interests, and educational goals. Our students have significant developmental, physical, communication, sensory, and behavioral needs. Teachers use a variety of instructional and communication approaches, including American Sign Language (ASL), spoken language, augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), voice-output systems, assistive technology, visual supports, and other multimodal communication strategies. Teachers work closely with a complete team of specialists, including Speech-Language Pathologists, Occupational Therapists, Physical Therapists, BCBAs, Assistive Technology Specialists, Adaptive Physical Education staff, Curriculum Specialists, and more.Key Responsibilities• Lead an early childhood classroom serving students with severe and complex disabilities• Deliver individualized, developmentally appropriate instruction aligned with student IEPs and educational goals• Adapt curriculum and instructional materials to meet students’ academic, developmental, communication, behavioral, sensory, and physical needs• Create a language-rich, communication-focused classroom environment that promotes engagement, independence, and meaningful participation• Implement the Massachusetts Curriculum Frameworks using a variety of evidence-based instructional strategies• Incorporate AAC, voice-output systems, assistive technology, visual supports, ASL, and other communication modalities throughout the school day• Collaborate closely with related-service providers and specialists to coordinate educational, therapeutic, behavioral, and communication supports• Participate in IEP development, educational assessments, progress monitoring, and required documentation• Develop and maintain strong partnerships with families and caregivers to support student success• Provide day-to-day guidance, support, and communication to classroom Teaching Assistants to ensure effective classroom functioning and student support• Participate in weekly professional development, collaborative planning, curriculum development, and ongoing learning opportunities• Foster a safe, respectful, and inclusive classroom environment aligned with CCCBSD’s mission and core valuesWhat We’re Looking For• Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university required; Master’s degree preferred• Must be eligible for Massachusetts DESE licensure or waiver as a Teacher of Students with Severe Disabilities; licensed candidates strongly preferred• Experience leading or supporting a classroom in a special education or early childhood setting strongly preferred• Experience working with children presenting with a range of disabilities and complex developmental needs required• Experience with or knowledge of AAC and voice-output communication systems required• Coursework or experience in Early Childhood Education, Special Education, Deaf Education, Communication Disorders, Assistive Technology, or related fields preferred• Familiarity with a variety of instructional methodologies and approaches for students with significant disabilities• Fluency in American Sign Language (ASL) strongly preferred; strong communication skills across modalities required• High comfort level implementing instructional technology and a range of language, academic, communication, and therapeutic supports• Ability to provide a supportive, caring, and student-centered learning environment• Strong collaboration, communication, and instructional leadership skills• Recent graduates and candidates who are eligible for Massachusetts licensure or a licensure waiver are encouraged to applyWhy Join CCCBSD?Live Our Values. Love Your Work.As a Certified Kindness Workplace, we believe that the workplace should be more than a place to achieve professional goals — it should be a space where compassion, respect, and empathy thrive. This culture of care creates a positive, supportive environment for students, families, and colleagues. Our work is grounded in CCCBSD’s core values: Humanity, Belonging, Inclusivity, Collaboration, Integrity, and Excellence.Why Educators Choose CCCBSDAt CCCBSD, we invest in our educators through meaningful support, professional growth, and a collaborative teaching environment designed to help both students and staff thrive.Exceptional Teaching Environment• Small classrooms with 3–5 students and strong classroom support• Weekly professional development and ongoing curriculum and clinical collaboration• Interdisciplinary team support throughout the school day• Language-rich, communication-first environment utilizing ASL, spoken language, AAC, and assistive technology• Specialized seven-acre campus in Beverly, MassachusettsCurrent Incentives for Eligible Candidates Include:• $3,000 sign-on bonus for eligible teachers hired for immediate openings• $2,500 Massachusetts licensure bonus for eligible out-of-state teachers upon obtaining MA licensure• Up to $1,500 relocation assistance for eligible candidates relocating to the areaCCCBSD’s Total Rewards Program Includes the Following Highlights:• 15+ PTO days annually, in addition to scheduled school breaks• Comprehensive medical and wellness benefits• Tuition reimbursement and ongoing in-service professional development• 401(k) retirement plan with a 5% employer match• Preschool discounts and free ASL classes• Employee referral and longevity bonus opportunities• Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) benefits, including up to 12 weeks of family leave and up to 20 weeks of medical leave, in accordance with Massachusetts state eligibility guidelines Starting salary for a first-year, Master’s-level licensed teacher is $79,036 annually, with additional compensation based on education and experience. As CCCBSD approaches 150 years of impact, we continue to honor our legacy of excellence while investing in the future of Deaf education through innovation, collaboration, and kindness. We hope you’ll find a professional home here — where your work matters, your values align, and your days are filled with purpose. Join us in making kindness the norm — and building a workplace where together, we truly thrive.Work Environment & Physical DemandsThis position involves active classroom participation and direct support of young children with diverse developmental, sensory, communication, behavioral, and physical needs. Responsibilities may include mobility assistance, feeding support, toileting, physical transfers, playground supervision, implementation of individualized care plans, and occasional administration of emergency medications in the absence of a nurse. Participation in emergency preparedness drills is required. Teachers must be able to actively engage in classroom activities, community-based instruction, and student support throughout the school day. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals to perform essential job functions. Located on a hill overlooking the scenic Bass River, our seven-acre campus sits at the corner of Echo Avenue and Route 62 in Beverly, MA — just 18 miles north of Boston and about 25 miles from Southern New Hampshire. Our peaceful, welcoming campus provides a beautiful environment for meaningful work and connection.Background Check RequirementEmployment is contingent upon the successful completion of all required background checks, including Massachusetts CORI and SAFIS fingerprinting, in accordance with state regulations.How to ApplyApply directly through this SchoolSpring posting or email questions to Jocelyn Clark, ECE Program Director, at jocelynclark@cccbsd.org. Not sure if you meet every qualification? We encourage you to apply — we value potential, lived experience, and a shared commitment to our mission.CCCBSD is an equal opportunity employer.We strongly encourage applications from individuals with multilingual backgrounds, lived experience, and/or ties to the communities we serve. If you require accommodations during the application or interview process, please contact us. We are committed to ensuring accessibility for all candidates. - WHERE COMMUNICATION COMES FIRST - Since 1876 - Learn more at www.cccbsd.org

Working as part of a collaborative classroom team, you will help create a safe, engaging, supportive environment where students can learn, communicate, develop independence, and thrive.Students may communicate through a variety of modalities, including spoken language, American Sign Language (ASL), assistive technology, and augmentative and alternative communication (AAC). jobs.description: Employer: Alpaca Health Expires: 10/30/2026 Alpaca HealthWork Location: In Person If you want work that challenges you, changes lives, and builds a real career, this is it. For many of our roles you don’t need your RBT certification to apply. What matters most is that you love working with kids, you’re dependable, and you’re ready to show up. Some roles do require an active certification, but if you’re not certified yet, we’ll help you find your path to getting there.Alpaca Health is a multi-state network of independent ABA therapists, working in homes, schools, and daycares. We hire certified RBTs and motivated people ready to become one. Either way, you’ll work alongside a dedicated BCBA who mentors you from day one, not a manager, not a corporate supervisor. Two ways to joinAlready an RBTActive RBT certificationStart working and earning right awayWork with clients in your regionA path toward BCBA if you want itNot certified yetA clear path to becoming an RBT, with a BCBA mentor from day oneMany practices in our network reimburse RBT training and pay you during hands-on learning, and we’ll help match you with the right fitSupport as you prepare for and sit for your certification exam The jobYou’ll work one-on-one with kids with autism in their homes, classrooms, and communities. Every day is different. You’ll follow a personalized plan from your BCBA, implement behavior strategies, collect data, and build the consistent relationships that help kids grow. Your BCBA is closely involved and reachable, so there’s no guessing and no flying solo. What’s in it for you:$20–$27/hour, based on experience and locationDirect mentorship from a dedicated BCBA, not managers or a corporate chain of commandFull-time or part-time (some flexibility across mornings, afternoons, and evenings is needed to meet client needs; not sure if a schedule fits? Just ask, we have many)Career growth support, including a path toward BCBA certificationDepending on the practice: training reimbursement and paid hands-on learning for those earning their certification You’re a good fit if you:Genuinely enjoy working with children, especially kids who need extra patience and creativityHave an active RBT certification, or the drive to earn oneHave reliable availability across mornings, afternoons, or evenings, since our clients count on consistencyCome from education, childcare, psychology, social work, or any role where you showed up for kidsHave reliable transportation to reach client homes and schoolsCan keep up physically, getting on the floor, moving around, staying active (able to lift ~50 lbs)Are at least 18, have a high school diploma or equivalent, and can pass a background check Why Alpaca HealthWe’re not a big clinic chain. jobs.title: Mental Health Clinician at Recovery Solutions
jobs.description: Employer: Recovery Solutions Expires: 10/30/2026 Location: BRIDGEWATER, MA 02324Pay Rate: $84,302.00 - $94,515.00 AnnuallyDepartment: Social ServicesDivision: Mental HealthJob Status: Full-TimeWork Shift: 8:00 AM - 4:30 PMDays Worked: Mon., Tue., Wed., Thu., Fri.Hour Per Week: 40Status: Accepting ApplicationsPosition Type: Full-TimeDetails: Bilingual Candidates are encouraged to apply!Position DescriptionAre you passionate about supporting individuals through mental health challenges and helping them achieve meaningful outcomes? We are seeking a Mental Health Clinician to join our multidisciplinary team and provide individualized clinical care, therapeutic interventions, and psychoeducation. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a collaborative, mission-driven environment and is committed to delivering high-quality, evidence-based mental health services. What You’ll Do Conduct clinical and psychosocial assessments for individuals served.Provide individual and group therapeutic interventions tailored to the population served.Deliver crisis assessment and intervention as needed.Document services and progress in compliance with legal, contractual, and regulatory requirements.Participate as an active member of the multidisciplinary team, contributing to treatment planning and discharge planning.Ensure treatment approaches are developmentally appropriate and aligned with individual needs. What We’re Looking For Education Master’s degree in Mental Health Counseling, Social Work, or Marriage and Family Therapy (required). Experience Two (2) years of experience with the population served (preferred). Licenses/Certifications Licensed or license-eligible in the appropriate discipline (required). Why Join Us? At our site, you’ll provide impactful mental health services while working in a supportive, team-oriented environment. You’ll have the opportunity to influence treatment outcomes, develop professionally, and make a tangible difference in the lives of the individuals we serve. Every day brings new challenges, learning opportunities, and the chance to create meaningful change. Apply today to join us as a Mental Health Clinician and help provide compassionate, high-quality care to the individuals we serve. Perks and Benefits In addition to comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, paid time off, and 401k, we foster a work, life balance for team members and their family to support physical, mental, and financial wellbeing, including: DailyPayTuition Assistance Employee Assistance Program (EAP) including free counseling and health coachingCompany paid life insuranceTax free Health Spending Accounts (HSA)Wellness program featuring fitness memberships and product discountsPet insuranceDiscount and reward programs for Theme Parks & Attractions, Hotels, Rental Cars, Water Parks, Virtual Events & Shows, Movie Tickets, Gift Cards, and more. *Eligibility for perks and benefits varies based on employee type and length of service. You Matter From top to bottom, we are a company of caregivers. If there is one unifying characteristic of everyone at Recovery Solutions, it is the deep desire to make a difference by helping society’s most vulnerable and often overlooked individuals. Every day our team has the distinct honor and responsibility to show up with non-judgmental compassion to provide hope and healing to those who need it most. For those of you whose calling it is to serve others, this is your moment. Your chance to join our family and be a part of our mission to care for those desperately in need, and to do your part to heal the world, one patient at a time. We encourage you to apply! If you are excited about a role but your experience doesn’t seem to align perfectly with every element of the job description, we encourage you to apply. You may be just the right candidate for this, or one of our many other roles. We are an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer We celebrate a variety of backgrounds and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Deadline to apply to this position is contingent upon applicant volume. Those positions located in Colorado will have a specific deadline posted in the job description. We are an Affirmative Action Employer in accordance with applicable state and local laws.

jobs.title: On-Call Substitute Teacher at Oakland Family Services
jobs.description: Employer: Oakland Family Services Expires: 10/30/2026 This is an On-Call Substitute Teacher position during the hours of 8:30am-4:30pm Monday through Friday based on your availability.Want to be a DIFFERENCE MAKER? Join our team and BUILD BRIGHTER FUTURES.WHY WORK FOR OAKLAND FAMILY SERVICES?We know that in order for you to do your best work and meet our mission, you must be able to be your best self. At Oakland Family Services (OFS), we care about our staff as people first. We treat our team members like family and understand the importance of their families at home. We recognize the significance of flexibility and work/life balance. We also know that your success…is our success. That’s why OFS not only honors the talent and experience you bring; we actively seek to develop it. Oakland Family Services has proudly been named a Top Workplace for over ten (10) years in a row, voted on by our own staff. We offer a warm, engaging, equitable, supportive, and inclusive work environment.ABOUT OAKLAND FAMILY SERVICESOakland Family Services is a private, non-profit service organization serving our community and building brighter futures for more than 100 years. We proudly offer a continuum of prevention, education and treatment services that span the human life cycle. OUR MISSION: Providing individuals and families the opportunity to build brighter futures. OUR VISION: Communities of thriving individuals and families. Between our strong commitment to our mission and a workplace culture that puts our staff first, we enrich the lives of those we serve, strengthen families, and build brighter futures for those we serve and those we employ. WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?Competitive compensation.Comprehensive medical, dental, prescription, and vision coverage.Flexible Spending Accounts and HSA options.Retirement plan with a company match.Long-term disability insurance.Voluntary short-term disability.Life insurance and AD&D.Malpractice insurance.Paid time off benefits, including generous vacation, sick, personal, and bereavement days.Twelve (12) paid holidays, including a floating holiday of your choice!Annual pay increases, as approved.Employee assistance program for you and immediate family.Network of support for your health & well-being.Verizon cellular plan discount.Mileage reimbursement at the IRS rate.Loan forgiveness programs.PLUS... Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.Family friendly practices and support.Flexible work schedules, as appropriate.Hybrid and virtual work options, as appropriate.Highly robust and comprehensive onboarding and training program.Paid professional development.Free online trainings that count toward continuing education credits.Employee assistance programs.“Dress for Your Day” approach to dress code.Financial literacy education and workshops.Collaborative annual performance appraisals.“Dollars for a Difference” program for clients and staff in need.And more!*Some benefits applicable to regular, full-time employees only.WE KNOW CULTURE MATTERS…We spend many hours of our day working. Workplace culture affects our well-being, how we feel about coming to work, and how we perform. Oakland Family Services prioritizes having a healthy, inclusive, equitable, and effective workplace culture. That’s why we proudly have twelve (12) defined cultural value statements that dictate how we operate. Cultural values are embedded into all we do and how we do it!…MORE ABOUT OUR AWARD-WINNING CULTUREOur CEO wants to get to know staff personally and has an open-door policy. She hosts regular staff lunches and townhalls to answer questions.Open, honest, and transparent communication is celebrated.We practice giving the benefit of the doubt.We believe that feedback is the breakfast of champions! That’s why we have a staff suggestion program.We want our team members to feel valued. That’s why we have a staff recognition program. Having FUN is an important part of the job! We love hosting events such as staff recognition celebrations and luncheons, road rallies, seasonal parties, food truck lunches, ice cream days, surprise giveaways, spirit weeks, Bring Your Child to Work Day, cook off/bake off contests, and more.ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY/WORKThe On-Call Substitute Teacher is responsible for supporting the overall day-to-day operations of a classroom in Oakland Family Services' Children's Learning Center (CLC) when the classroom teachers are absent. The on-call substitute teacher is responsible for assisting with the implementation of high quality, HighScope learning experiences for children, daily lesson planning, interacting with parents and volunteers, record keeping, and other miscellaneous operations related to the Children's Learning Center Programs. This position is a as needed, on call position. The position reports to the Early Childhood Education Site Supervisor. Assist in implementing and evaluating developmentally appropriate, engaging activities using the HighScope approach to learning with children.Maintain standards of quality as required by State licensure, Great Start to Quality and NAEYC accreditation.Assist in maintaining accurate records of the children's attendance, meal records, incident reports, medication for children, allergies, and sign-in/out sheets for parents.Participate in daily team planning meetings to create daily lesson plans and coordinate task responsibilities.Participate in Agency and program activities.Assist with daily documentation of children's interactions and play through anecdotal notes.Assist in the creation and implementation of children’s behavioral support plans as needed.Maintain the arrangement, appearance and cleanliness of the learning environment.Supervise and ensure the health, safety and well-being of each child.Participate in professional development opportunities as required by the Agency, licensing and funding requirements.Responsible for incorporating principles of diversity, equity and inclusion in work processes and in job functions. Responsible for promoting a feeling of welcoming, belonging, and acceptance to all clients and staff.Other duties as assigned.Physical DemandsWhile performing the duties of the job, the employee is regularly required to be physical and capable of successfully managing an early learning environment. The employee is frequently required to sit and/or stand for 8 hours or more. Staff must have the ability to reach with hands and arms and must occasionally lift and move up to 25 pounds. Does this Describe YOU?Must possess at minimum a High School Diploma or equivalent.Proper training in Early Childhood Education, including, but not limited to, a Child Development Associate Credential (CDA) associate’s degree in child development or related field or equivalent continuing education experience as approved by the Michigan Department of Education.A minimum of one year of preschool teaching experience is preferred.Experience with the HighScope approach preferred.Communication skills that focus on positive and professional communication with parents and children.Utilization of positive management techniques in the classroom.Abilities and skills in the team approach to problem solving and task completion.Shows sensitivity to cultural differences.Other relevant qualifications that support positive performance in the position.Selected candidates for this position must possess a sensitivity to the diversity of the agency’s service population including (but not limited to) differences of culture, race, religion, gender, sexual orientation and socioeconomic.Special abilities and skills necessary to perform the required tasks and that best meet the needs of the agency also will be considered. There may be some standards above that may be waived when compensating specifications or circumstances exist.

jobs.title: Lead Toddler and Early Preschool Teacher at The Goddard School - Chicago, IL - South Loop
jobs.description: Employer: The Goddard School - Chicago, IL - South Loop Expires: 10/30/2026 The Goddard School of South Loop – Chicago, ILFull-Time Part-Time. | Lead Teacher(s) Do you love working with young children, take pride in your classroom, and want to work at a school where great teachers are valued and supported? The Goddard School of South Loop is looking for experienced and passionate Lead Teachers for our Toddler and Early Preschool classrooms. We believe children thrive when they are surrounded by teachers who are nurturing, dependable, engaged and genuinely excited to help them grow. We also believe great teachers deserve a workplace that invests in them. Our goal is to build a team of educators who don't simply supervise children—we want teachers who build relationships, create meaningful learning experiences, take ownership of their classrooms, support their teammates, and continue growing professionally. What You'll Do As a Lead Teacher, you will take an active leadership role in your classroom and help create a safe, loving and engaging environment for children. You will: Build warm, trusting relationships with children and familiesProvide attentive, active supervision throughout the dayPlan and implement engaging, developmentally appropriate learning experiencesCreate a classroom environment where children can explore, learn and develop independenceObserve children's development and individual needsMaintain regular classroom documentation and family communicationEstablish consistent classroom routines and positive guidance practicesKeep your classroom organized, welcoming and prepared for learningWork collaboratively with supporting teachers and provide classroom leadership and directionParticipate in school events, professional development and team initiativesPartner with our leadership team when challenges arise rather than feeling like you have to solve everything alone The Teacher We're Looking For We're especially interested in educators who: Genuinely enjoy spending their day with young childrenAre warm, patient and nurturingUnderstand that active supervision and children's safety come firstTake ownership of their classroom rather than waiting to be told what needs to be doneAre dependable and understand how much their attendance matters to children and their teammatesCommunicate professionally with families, coworkers and leadershipAre comfortable receiving feedback and interested in continuing to growWork well as part of a teamBring positive energy and solutions when challenges ariseUnderstand that teaching young children involves much more than completing a lesson plan—it is about relationships, engagement, observation and purposeful interactions throughout the entire day You do not need to know everything on Day One. We value teachers who are willing to learn, receptive to coaching and committed to becoming stronger educators. What You Can Expect From Us We know that taking care of children begins with taking care of the people who teach them. At The Goddard School of South Loop, we strive to create an environment where teachers feel supported, appreciated and able to grow. Depending on eligibility and position, our team members may receive: Competitive compensation based on education and experiencePaid time offPaid holidaysHealth and other eligible benefits401(k) benefitsChildcare benefits/discountsProfessional development and training opportunitiesSupport with continuing education and credential advancementOpportunities for increased responsibility and career growthClassroom resources and curriculum supportRegular appreciation and recognition throughout the yearAn accessible leadership team that is actively involved in the schoolWe believe good work should be noticed. We regularly recognize team members who demonstrate exceptional commitment, teamwork, professional growth and care for our children and families. A School Where Teachers Can Grow Our leadership team believes in coaching, not simply correcting. We understand that early childhood education can be demanding. When something isn't working, our goal is to identify the challenge, provide resources and support, and help our teachers become successful. At the same time, because families entrust us with their children every day, we hold ourselves to high standards for safety, professionalism, reliability and accountability. If you are looking for a school where you can simply "watch kids," this probably isn't the right position. But if you want to be part of a school where your work matters, where you can develop as an educator, and where strong teachers are genuinely valued, we would love to meet you. Qualifications Ideal candidates will have: Experience working with toddlers and/or preschool-age childrenEarly Childhood Education coursework, degree, CDA or equivalent qualifications preferredAbility to meet Illinois DCFS Lead Teacher requirements for the assigned classroomStrong communication and teamwork skillsAbility to meet the physical requirements of an early childhood classroomCommitment to maintaining all licensing, health and safety requirements Experienced Assistant Teachers who meet Lead Teacher qualifications and are ready to take the next step in their career are also encouraged to apply. Join Our Goddard Village The relationships our teachers build with children can last for years. Many of our families begin with us during infancy and remain through Pre-K, giving our educators the opportunity to watch children grow from babies into confident kindergarteners.We take that responsibility—and that privilege—seriously.If you're an educator who wants to make an impact, continue growing, and be part of a supportive school community, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and tell us a little about what you love most about working with young children. Note: Candidate must be CO-VID vaccinated.Compensation: $19.00 - $24.00 per hour

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Behavioral Youth Counselor - Memphis, TN at Youth Villages
jobs.description: Employer: Youth Villages Expires: 10/30/2026 Program Overview:Youth Villages' residential programs in Tennessee and Georgia provide safe, nurturing environments for youth ages 6 to 17 with complex behavioral and mental health challenges. These programs are offered across three types of facilities—secure facilities, open campuses, and group homes—each designed to meet the individual needs of youth exhibiting a range of referral behaviors, including aggression, self-harm, suicidal ideations, and problem sexual behavior. Our residential campuses deliver an intensive treatment program that strikes a unique balance between structure and freedom, all while preparing youth for continued success outside of a residential setting. A key focus is to help each youth step down to the least restrictive treatment option possible by developing the skills they need to thrive in less structured environments through trauma-informed care, clinical interventions, life skills building, and recreation therapy (in selection locations). Most youth also attend fully accredited schools located on our campuses, ensuring their educational progress continues alongside therapeutic support. Essential Duties and Responsibilities:The Behavioral Youth Counselor, also known as a Teacher Counselor:Teaches youth necessary life skills and provides for their daily physical careAssists in treatment planning for each youthParticipates in youth transports to various locations (including but not limited to doctors' appointments, court dates, community outings, home passes, etc.)Participates in recreation therapy sessions with their assigned group of youthHelps youth develop and implement positive coping skills using therapeutic interventionsFacilitates group therapy sessions to support youth building life skills, social skills, moral reasoning skills, and anger control skillsCompletes daily documentation (such as contact notes, milieu notes, and precautionary notes) in an electronic medical record system (EMR)Performs other duties as assigned Schedule:This position works on a non-traditional schedule and requires flexibility as it includes evening and weekend shifts. Behavioral Youth Counselors follow a Sun–Wed or Wed–Sat rotation, generally working between 12:00 PM–10:30 PM, and the weekend day may include a 16-hour shift based on campus staffing models. All roles require at least 40 hours per week, with overtime at time and a half for additional hours. Specific campus schedules and rotation details will be discussed with the hiring manager in the interview process, and any adjustments for training or coverage will be communicated ahead of time. Additional Information:The supervision and treatment of youth requires prolonged periods of walking, standing, running, climbing stairs, and physical agility. Applicants must be able to participate in physical interventions when necessary and frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, occasionally more than 100 pounds.Applicants are required to complete Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI) and CPR trainings and pass an agility and strength evaluation.Applicants must possess a current, valid driver’s license Compensation:Average annual salary ranges from $54,000 to $64,000, depending on schedule and hours worked. Time-and-a-half pay is provided for worked holidays. Qualifications:Bachelor's degree (required)Experience working with at-risk youth and/or families (strongly preferred)Experience working with youth (required)Strong organizational skills and attention to detailExcellent written, verbal, and oral skillsAbility to manage multiple priorities simultaneouslyBasic computer knowledgeAbility to maintain a flexible schedule

jobs.description: Employer: Youth Villages Expires: 10/30/2026 Program Overview: Intercept®, developed by Youth Villages, is an evidence-based intensive, in-home program that focuses on keeping families together by preventing out-of-home placements or facilitating reunification after such placements, including foster care, residential treatment facilities, hospitalization, or juvenile detention centers. It is one of the first programs to receive the well-supported designation from Title IV-E Prevention Services Clearinghouse developed in accordance with the Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA) having been shown to reduce out-of-home placements and accelerate permanency for children.This program serves youth from birth to age 18 who are facing serious emotional or behavioral challenges or have experienced trauma, such as abuse or neglect. Services are provided by highly trained Family Intervention Specialists directly in the family’s home and community–Intercept® is not an office-based program.Intercept provides intensive, strength-based support tailored to each family’s unique needs, ultimately helping them achieve lasting change through evidence-based mental health interventions, along with the development of new parenting and communication skills. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: The Family Intervention Specialist:Carries a caseload of 4 to 6 familiesHolds individual and family sessions with each family 3 times a week, scheduled at the convenience of the familiesConducts on-going assessment of youth to determine their needs from a strength-focused, solution-based perspectiveAttends 3 weekly meetings (individual, team, and clinical consultation) for professional development to help enhance clinical skillsDrives up to 60 to 80 miles to meet with families in their homes and communities (additional travel may be required)Collaborates with other providers, case workers, and courts to formulate a collaborative treatment planProvides on-call crisis support to the youth and family (schedules vary by location)Completes accurate and timely documentation in an electronic medical record system (EMR)Performs other duties as assigned Additional Information:Schedule is flexible and non-traditional as it is based around the availability of youth and families served.Applicants must possess a current, valid driver’s license, an automobile for work purposes, and proof of auto insurance.Community-based staff will be reimbursed for applicable mileage. jobs.description: Employer: Cornell College Expires: 10/30/2026 Cornell College invites applications for an Associate Director, Berry Career Institute. The Associate Director directly serves students and plays an important role in the day-to-day operations of the Berry Career Institute. The Berry Career Institute (BCI) is part of the division of Alumni and College Advancement, positioning career outcomes as a central strategic priority that connects the student experience to graduate careers, alumni engagement, and the long-term reputation of a Cornell College education. The Associate Director coaches students, facilitates programs, and contributes to the broader career-learning initiatives of the college to ensure that all students are given opportunities to develop the skills and perspective needed to navigate the world of work and apply their liberal arts education beyond the classroom.Duties and ResponsibilitiesStudent & Alumni Career Coaching: Primarily serves as the point of contact for a portfolio of current students and alumni to provide career coaching and professional development support in individual and group settings. Creates and maintains career coaching resources and materials. Develops opportunities to connect alumni to current students through networking and mentoring. Stays up-to-date on industry and employer trends to help students navigate a changing employment landscape and best apply their liberal arts education to their life beyond Cornell College.Program Facilitation: Designs, facilitates, and promotes a variety of programs with internal and external partners to increase career-readiness, vocational discernment, professional development, and related skills among students across the College. Programs may include workshops and trainings inside the classroom in partnership with faculty, or programs may include events outside of the classroom such as tablings, large-scale expos or fairs, panels, guest speakers, webinars, or off campus trips such as employer tours.Experiential Learning Development: Contributes to the development and implementation of an internship program for students by identifying and cultivating relationships with potential employer partners. Develops experiential learning opportunities for students with employers. Directs students in how to find and secure internships. Helps students fund and document their experiential learning through Cornell College’s Ingenuity in Action program.Data Management and Reporting: Helps maintain information systems (i.e. Handshake) to ensure the BCI accurately tracks student and employer engagement as well as career-related learning outcomes. Contributes to the development and assessment of career learning outcomes. Sources student outcomes for priority reports such as the First Destination Survey. Identifies stories and qualitative data to be shared in BCI and College reporting and marketing.Campus-Wide Support: Serves on workgroups and supports campus-wide initiatives by collaborating with faculty and campus partners to advance career-readiness and experiential learning throughout the curriculum and College culture.Other Duties as AssignedQualification and Education RequirementsBachelor's degree is required. Master’s degree or other training related to higher education administration, student development, counseling, or another area relevant to student engagement is preferred. Previous experience with career development and work in a college setting is preferred. Must possess a valid Iowa driver’s license and be insurable to drive.Preferred SkillsEvidence of strong interpersonal and written and verbal communication skills, including facilitation skills such as designing and leading content for a variety of audiences and learning stylesKnowledge of student development practices (prior student advising or coaching and mentoring experience a plus)Organization and planning skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and constituents, including event planning and program development and assessmentStrong team player with the ability to collaborate effectively across departmentsUnderstanding of data management best practices and attention to detailDedication to liberal arts educationAwareness of human resources, recruitment, and hiring practicesWork Location & ConditionsWork is performed primarily while seated in an office environment. Some walking from building to building on campus is needed to attend various meetings. Employees may be required to perform other job-related duties as assigned. All requirements are subject to change over time, with possible modifications made to reasonably accommodate individuals with a disability.Cornell College offers a fantastic benefits package that includes health, dental, vision, HSA & FSA accounts, a TIAA 403(b) retirement account, and tuition remission and exchange for employees and dependents. The hiring pay range for this position is $42,000 - $48,000. Application ProcessTo apply, submit a resume, cover letter, and list of at least three professional references through Cornell College's online application system.Cornell is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from underrepresented groups. jobs.title: Student Success Coach and Mentor, AmeriCorps Member ( 2027-2028 term) at City Year
jobs.description: Employer: City Year Expires: 10/30/2026 About City Year City Year, an AmeriCorps program, helps students across schools succeed. Teams of City Year AmeriCorps members provide support to students, classrooms and the whole school, helping to ensure that students in schools receive a high-quality education that prepares them with the skills and mindset to thrive and contribute to their community. What You’ll Do As a City Year AmeriCorps member, your service will focus on coaching and mentoring elementary, middle and/or high school students. You will help these students earn academic success, improve their attendance, and develop positive behaviors at school. You will plan and monitor individual student progress and work with teachers on whole class instruction, breakout spaces and other in-class student assistance. Role and Responsibilities Experience in all these tasks is not necessary. We provide 1-4 weeks of training at the beginning of the year to support you. Plus, you will work with partner teachers and school staff every step of the way. Support academic coaching and interpersonal development for students: Work with identified students 1:1 and in small groups Develop literacy and/or math skills varying learning activities by student level, answering student questions and encouraging assignment completion Develop interpersonal skills throughout their day, using proven strategies of learning, practicing, reflection and repetition Collaborate with teachers and team members to collect, record, analyze and monitor individual student progress, participating in facilitated reviews of student data collected and entered into City Year’s student data system Create an engaging, safe and healthy classroom space in collaboration with the teacher Support Whole School initiatives to increase engagement with students and families: Support and/or conduct extended day and virtual programming for students before, during and after school including, but not limited to, academic enrichment and intervention, homework support, recreation and student clubs, service learning, and leadership development Create, support and/or co-lead events or programs that recognize and appreciate student growth and/or achievement in math, literacy, attendance, and behavior City Year benefits You will receive: Bi-weekly living stipend Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance Curalinc Employee Assistance Program Talkspace Therapy Program Free 3-year membership to Happier Meditation AppWorkers’ compensation Relocation support Benefits specific to City Year location Career and University partnerships and scholarships City Year / AmeriCorps Uniform parts AmeriCorps and other federally issued benefits You will be eligible for: Segal AmeriCorps Education Award Child care benefits paid by AmeriCorps Loan forbearance and interest accrual payments for qualified student loans Eligibility Requirements City Year AmeriCorps members are as varied as the communities we serve. We’re looking for you if you want to build yourself, give back and are ready to change the world. Be a U.S. citizen or legal permanent resident (Authorization to work in the U.S. is not sufficient. Those with DACA status unfortunately are not eligible at this time) Be 17-25 by July 1, 2027Have a GED or high school diploma, some college experience, or college degree Have served no more than three terms in an AmeriCorps state or national program* Agree to and complete a background check Be able to begin City Year by July/August 2027 (specific start date varies by location) How to Apply City Year accepts applications on a rolling admissions basis, however our deadlines to apply are Oct 30th, Feb 12th, April 3rd and May 14th. As such, this is a continuous position posting. To learn about our application process, complete this quick form to get connected with a City Year Recruiter.

jobs.title: Golf Instruction Intern at Apex Park and Recreation District
jobs.description: Employer: Apex Park and Recreation District Expires: 10/30/2026 Job Title: Intern – Golf InstructionDepartment: Golf Operations – Indian Tree Golf ClubSupervisor’s Title: Director of Golf and Clubhouse Operations/ Golf Instruction ProfessionalDate Prepared: 9/2026 Job Status: Part-Time, Non-Exempt POSITION PURPOSE: Supports golf instruction, player development, and related golf programming at Indian Tree Golf Club. Works alongside professional golf staff to gain hands-on experience assisting with junior and adult instruction, clinics, camps, individual lessons, player-development programs, and on-course instruction. Provides support for the administrative and operational responsibilities associated with delivering quality golf programming at a public golf facility. This internship is designed to provide meaningful professional development for an individual interested in pursuing a career in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, or the golf industry. ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Assists golf professionals with individual and group golf instruction for participants of varying ages and skill levels. Supports junior golf camps and clinics, adult programs, beginner programs, and other player-development initiatives. Assists with instruction in putting, chipping, pitching, bunker play, full swing, course management, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Prepares instructional areas, equipment, training aids, range balls, and other materials prior to programs and lessons. Assists with participant check-in, group organization, instructional stations, and program transitions. Provides basic instructional feedback to participants under the direction of professional golf staff. Assists with on-course instruction on the Par-3 and regulation golf courses. Helps create a positive, encouraging, safe, and welcoming learning environment for golfers of different ages, abilities, skill levels, and backgrounds. Assists with adaptive golf and other programs designed to make golf accessible to a broad range of participants. Assists staff in developing golf clinics, camps, leagues, lesson plans, instructional activities, and other player-development opportunities. Helps evaluate existing programs and identifies opportunities to improve the participant experience. Supports player-development efforts for juniors, beginners, women, seniors, and other developing golfers. Assists with utilizing the driving range, practice facilities, and Par-3 course as player-development resources. Assists with program registration, participation tracking, attendance, participant feedback, and program evaluation. Supports marketing and communication efforts related to golf programs and instructional opportunities. Maintains clean, organized, safe, and professional instructional and practice areas. Consistently represents the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work when interacting with participants, guests, and coworkers. OTHER DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:Gains exposure to golf shop operations, outside operations, tee-sheet management, pace of play, tournament operations, customer service, and daily golf course operations. Learns policies and procedures related to golf instruction, course access, range operations, safety, and guest service. Gains an understanding of golf program pricing, budgeting, revenue generation, expense management, and other business aspects of operating a public golf facility. Assists with golf shop and outside operations as assigned to gain a broader understanding of golf facility operations. Works with professional golf staff to establish internship learning goals and participates in ongoing coaching and feedback. May be given increasing responsibility for planning and delivering portions of clinics or instructional programs under the supervision of professional golf staff. Develops practical experience in golf instruction and coaching techniques, junior and adult programming, player development, customer service and hospitality, program management and evaluation, and public-sector golf operations. Performs other duties as assigned. SUPERVISORY DUTIES: This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. May assist with organizing and directing participants during camps, clinics, lessons, and other instructional activities under the supervision of professional golf staff. JOB QUALIFICATIONS -KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, etiquette, and pace of play. Interest in golf instruction, player development, golf operations, and the golf industry. Ability to effectively communicate with children, adults, guests, and coworkers. Strong customer service and interpersonal skills. Ability to create a positive and welcoming experience for program participants. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Ability to follow direction and work within the scope of assigned responsibilities and training. Ability and willingness to learn, accept coaching and feedback, and demonstrate initiative.Ability to maintain a professional appearance and demeanor. Ability to prioritize participant, guest, and employee safety. Ability to organize equipment and instructional materials and assist with multiple activities and participant groups. Ability to work a flexible schedule that may include mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays. Ability to consistently demonstrate the principles of the Indian Tree Way – Intentional Hospitality, Operational Excellence, and Making It Work. EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Interest in golf instruction, PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, coaching, or a related field. Working knowledge of golf fundamentals, rules, and etiquette. Experience or demonstrated ability working effectively with children and adults. CPR/AED/First Aid certification or ability to obtain certification as required.Preferred Qualifications: Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a PGA Golf Management, recreation, sports management, education, kinesiology, business, or related program. Previous experience working at a golf course, driving range, golf camp, recreation program, or instructional setting. Previous experience working with children or youth programs. Interest in pursuing PGA membership or a career in golf instruction, player development, or golf operations.WORK ENVIRONMENT: Work is performed in both indoor and outdoor environments at Indian Tree Golf Club, including the golf shop, driving range, practice facilities, Par-3 course, and regulation golf courses. Work may be performed in varying weather and environmental conditions. The position requires regular interaction with children, adults, program participants, guests, and other employees in an active public recreation environment.PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES: Position requires the ability to stand and walk for extended periods, including walking on uneven outdoor terrain and golf course surfaces. Requires frequent bending, reaching, and movement associated with demonstrating golf skills, setting up instructional areas, and assisting with programs. Must be able to handle, move, and set up golf equipment, training aids, range balls, and other instructional materials and equipment. TRAVEL: Limited travel may be required for meetings, training, programs, or other District-related activities. NOTE: This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the job. May perform other duties as assigned.
